questions.stem: The first step in hardening a new server is:

choices.D: Removing or disabling all unnecessary services, ports, and default accounts

questions.explanation: Hardening starts by reducing the attack surface, removing unused services, applications, and default accounts before adding additional controls.

choices.B: Prescriptive consensus-based security configuration guidelines for specific systems and applications
choices.C: A vulnerability scoring system for CVEs

questions.explanation: CIS Benchmarks give specific, tested configuration recommendations (disable SMBv1, enable audit logging, enforce password policy) for systems including Windows, Linux, and cloud platforms.

choices.A: Only known malware with matching signatures
choices.D: Novel malware by detecting suspicious behaviours like code injection and unusual network connections

questions.explanation: Behavioural/heuristic detection monitors what code does rather than what it looks like, enabling detection of new or modified malware bypassing signatures.

choices.A: Default allow, block only known bad applications
choices.B: Reputation scoring of applications before execution
choices.C: Sandbox all unknown applications before execution
choices.D: Default deny, only pre-approved applications are permitted to execute

questions.explanation: Allowlisting is default-deny: only specifically approved applications may run. All unapproved applications, including novel malware, are blocked.

choices.A: Physical theft of a device or removal of its storage drive
choices.B: Malware executing on a running system

questions.explanation: FDE makes data unreadable without the decryption key. Physical possession of the stolen drive does not expose the data.

choices.A: All users share a single admin account
choices.B: Admin accounts can only be used at the physical console
choices.C: No user may install any software
choices.D: Users run as standard accounts daily; admin credentials used only when specifically required

questions.explanation: Least privilege limits daily-use accounts to standard (non-admin) rights. Administrative actions require separate elevation, limiting malware damage.

questions.stem: EDR extends traditional antivirus by providing:

choices.B: Continuous telemetry, behavioural analysis, automated containment, and investigation capabilities
choices.C: Network-level packet inspection for all endpoint traffic

questions.explanation: EDR provides continuous endpoint visibility, behavioural detection, automated response (isolation, process kill), and investigation tools beyond what traditional AV offers.

choices.A: Network traffic at a switch port
choices.C: Activity on individual endpoint systems including file changes, processes, and log entries

questions.explanation: HIDS monitors individual hosts from within, watching process activity, file system changes, registry modifications, and log entries to detect local attacks.

questions.stem: MDM remote wipe is used to:

choices.C: Remove corporate or all data from a lost or stolen device

questions.explanation: Remote wipe removes data from lost or stolen devices. Selective wipe removes only corporate data while preserving personal data, important for BYOD.

questions.stem: OS patching is a primary defence against:
questions.explanation: Patches fix known vulnerabilities. Unpatched systems remain exploitable by tools targeting documented CVEs that may be public for months or years.
